reason: I fetched the Van Gogh Museum translation of letter 528 and read section 2v:6: both sentences stand verbatim, in the order claimed, immediately after 'And I have at least embarked on it and have laid certain foundations, which isn't exactly the easiest part of the job!', with the same curly apostrophes in I've and can't; the site's own italics on what I can't do yet are the only thing dropped, which is a typographic loss, not a wording change. The header confirms Anthon van Rappard, Nuenen, on or about Tuesday, 18 August 1885, and the old Complete Letters number R57, so the locator is right. One real defect: rule 30 asks a translated line to name the translator, and 'trans. Van Gogh Museum edition, 2009' names an edition. The edition's credits page thanks 'coordinating editor Michael Hoyle, responsible for the English manuscript, and the distinguished translators Sue Dyson, Imogen Forster, Lynne Richards, John Rudge and Diane Webb', and publishes no per-letter translator, so no single name can honestly be given; the nearest honest fix is in betterCitation and it still fits 140 characters. Second, smaller: the page I read is the web edition marked 'Version: December 2024', which carries the 2009 edition's authorized translations, and the printed 2009 volume was not opened. For the note, the famous English form of this line, 'I am always doing what I cannot do yet, in order to learn how to do it', is the older Complete Letters rendering of this same sentence in R57, so a reader who knows the line by heart will meet different words on the card and the note should say why. Attribution is not in the misattribution list; shipped.js returns no match, no near match, Van Gogh at 0 of 3, not banned; tag Correspondence is the form of the work; scope, publishability and the theme (the road that teaches, making what he cannot do yet in order to learn it) all hold; source 124 characters, leads with the name, no dash.
betterCitation: Vincent van Gogh, The Letters, no. 528, to Anthon van Rappard, Nuenen, 18 August 1885 (trans. Michael Hoyle and others, 2009)
